# MindsHub by MindsDB

> MindsHub is the platform for open-source AI agents — where they live, learn, and get things done. Delegate tasks through Cowork, the unified workspace, or run any agent with its native harness.

## Core pages

### MindsHub
URL: https://mindshub.ai/

MindsHub is the platform for open-source AI agents — where they live and do real work. The home experience is Cowork, the unified workspace: brief a whole task in plain language and collect what the agent produces — documents, dashboards, apps, reports — instead of a bare chat box. Cowork connects your data and tools through a connectors directory and a credentials vault (the agent never sees raw keys), lets you choose models from a dropdown (a planning model and a coding model, routed through MindsHub), turns agent output into real artifacts you can publish to a live URL, and organizes work into projects you can share. It also keeps memory across sessions, a reusable skill library, and scheduled tasks. Cowork runs on interchangeable open-source agents — Anton and Hermes today, with more to come — and you can switch the agent harness or the model from a dropdown without losing context. Builders can also run agents like OpenClaw, OpenClaw + GBrain, and NanoClaw standalone with their native harnesses. $9.95/month — cancel anytime. Cowork runs on the web (no install) or as a desktop app for macOS and Windows — both installers are linked from the homepage at mindshub.ai.

Q: What is MindsHub Cowork?
A: MindsHub Cowork is the unified workspace for open-source agents — one place for every agent and model. Brief a whole task in plain language, connect your data and tools, and collect finished, shareable work. The agent and model are swappable underneath.

Q: Which agents power Cowork?
A: Cowork runs on interchangeable open-source agent harnesses — Anton and Hermes today, with more on the way. Anton is the default; switch the harness and the model from a dropdown anytime. Picking a different agent per individual task is coming soon.

Q: Can I switch the agent or model?
A: You can switch the agent harness and the model from a dropdown today — the change applies across your work, not to one task at a time. Choosing a different agent per task is coming soon, along with memory that follows you across agents.

Q: Do I need to pick a model or agent to start?
A: No. Create an account and brief your first task — there are no agent, model, or API-key decisions to make first. Sensible defaults are set for you, and you can switch the model or harness anytime.

Q: Why isn't a chat box enough for an AI agent?
A: Chat is good for a question and an answer. Real knowledge work needs connected data, the right model for each step, a place for results to live, and a way to share them. Cowork is the workspace around the agent, not just a transcript.

Q: How does Cowork connect to my data?
A: Through a connectors directory and a credentials vault. You connect sources like databases, warehouses, and SaaS tools once; secrets stay in the vault, scoped per connection, and the agent never sees a raw key.

Q: Is there a desktop or mobile app?
A: Cowork runs on the web with nothing to install, and ships as a desktop app for macOS and Windows — both installers are linked on the homepage. Mobile apps are coming soon.

Q: How do I get started?
A: Create an account and brief your first task — no agent, model, or runtime to pick first. $9.95/month, cancel anytime, on the web or the desktop app.

### About
URL: https://mindshub.ai/about

We're on a mission to democratize access to AI. Co-founders Jorge Torres and Adam Carrigan released the first MindsDB code in 2018 in Berkeley, California — inspired by Iain M. Banks' Culture novels and the idea that AI works best as a partner that augments human judgment. The breakthrough principle was simple: don't make data teams adopt new tools — bring the AI to the systems where the data already lives. That principle built an open-source community of 800+ contributors and 39,000+ GitHub stars; the same principle now powers MindsHub for AI agents. The company has raised $50M+ from Benchmark, Mayfield, Y Combinator, and NVIDIA. The team is international by design — distributed across North America, Europe, the Middle East, South America, and Asia Pacific. Four values hold across every product surface: open source first, democratizing access to AI, bringing AI to the data, and model neutrality.

Q: What is MindsHub?
A: MindsHub is the platform for open-source AI agents — where they live, learn, and get things done. You delegate whole tasks through Cowork, the unified workspace, and collect finished, shareable work, or run any open-source agent with its native UI and harness. MindsHub is built by MindsDB.

Q: Is MindsHub the same as MindsDB?
A: MindsHub is the product; MindsDB is the company behind it. In 2026 we renamed the agent platform from MindsDB to MindsHub, because the old name implied a database. Same company, same team, same mission — only the product name changed.

Q: Is MindsHub open source?
A: Yes. The core that powers MindsHub is open-source — github.com/mindsdb/minds — and the agents it runs are open-source too. Inspect them, run them locally, or run them on MindsHub with no lock-in.

Q: Who is MindsHub for?
A: Knowledge workers — including technical ones — who want whole tasks off their plate, and developers or teams who run their own open-source agents. Most people start in Cowork; builders run their agent from the console.

Q: Who builds MindsHub?
A: MindsHub is built by MindsDB, founded in 2018 in Berkeley by Jorge Torres and Adam Carrigan. MindsDB is backed by Benchmark, Mayfield, Y Combinator, and NVIDIA, with a global open-source community of 800+ contributors.

### Agents
URL: https://mindshub.ai/agents

MindsHub hosts five open-source agents. OpenClaw is the production workhorse — multi-step planning, deep tool use, long-running execution. OpenClaw + GBrain is the same workhorse with a persistent local memory layer (GBrain) so context survives across sessions. NanoClaw is the small, fast sibling for short jobs and embedded triggers. Anton is the open-source AI coworker — hand it an outcome in plain language and collect finished, shareable work. Hermes is the orchestration agent that moves information between systems and drives multi-step workflows. All five run on the same always-on cloud runtime with the Model Router across commercial and open models. Cowork adds a credentials vault, connectors, and a scratchpad; OpenClaw + GBrain adds a persistent brain; each agent keeps its own memory. The agents are open-source and can be run locally; MindsHub is the managed option.

### OpenClaw
URL: https://mindshub.ai/agents/openclaw

OpenClaw is the production-ready open agent. It calls tools, executes code, plans across many steps, and works through real integrations — good for multi-step automations across SaaS, internal copilots, long workflows over databases and APIs, and domain-specific agents you own end-to-end. On MindsHub it runs with the Model Router and an always-on cloud runtime, native harness intact — the same agent you can self-host, with the operational backbone managed for you. Layer on OpenClaw + GBrain when you want a persistent memory that compounds.

### OpenClaw + GBrain
URL: https://mindshub.ai/agents/openclaw-gbrain

OpenClaw + GBrain pairs the open-source workhorse agent with GBrain (github.com/garrytan/gbrain), a local memory layer for agents. The brain is a structured store of pages, facts, and entities the agent reads from before answering and writes to as it works — so the agent gets sharper week over week instead of starting from scratch every session. On MindsHub it ships as a 1-click deploy: each user gets an isolated instance with GBrain pre-installed (pinned to a verified upstream release), a 43-skill skillpack pre-scaffolded, PGLite as the local brain backend, and the MindsHub Model Router pre-configured. Good for long-running engagements where context matters (customer success, account management, research projects), personal AI coworkers that learn your world, knowledge accumulation across teams, and founder/operator copilots that remember your investors, customers, and team's history without re-priming.

### NanoClaw
URL: https://mindshub.ai/agents/nanoclaw

NanoClaw is OpenClaw's small, fast sibling. Use it for short, well-scoped jobs: webhook handlers, scheduled micro-jobs, single-purpose extractors and classifiers, fast prototypes. On MindsHub NanoClaw runs on the same always-on cloud runtime and Model Router as OpenClaw — but with a lighter footprint and economics that suit short jobs. Drop-in upgrade path to OpenClaw when the work outgrows the shape.

### Anton
URL: https://mindshub.ai/agents/anton

Anton is a different shape of agent. You don't prompt it; you hand it an outcome. "Pull this week's revenue, explain the biggest movers, and ship a dashboard" comes back as a published dashboard, a written explanation, and a transparent trace of every SQL query and Python step it ran. You work with Anton in Cowork, the unified workspace for open agents — Cowork runs Anton and Hermes today, with more harnesses on the way. Connect your data and tools through a secure vault, brief the task in plain language, and collect the artifacts. Open by design: switch the model underneath anytime and keep everything you build. $9.95/month, cancel anytime, 5M tokens included, no API keys to start. The use-cases gallery at /use-cases shows 36 concrete handoffs across ops, data, GTM, product, finance, and research.

### Hermes
URL: https://mindshub.ai/agents/hermes

Hermes is the messenger agent. It listens for events, transforms what it hears into the right shape for the next destination, and routes information where it needs to go — workflow orchestration across SaaS, automated digests and briefings, system-to-system bridges, multi-step pipelines. On MindsHub it runs 24/7 on the cloud runtime with its native harness, picks the model per step via the Router, and orchestrates multi-step work across your systems — routing each step where it needs to go instead of following fixed rules.

### Use cases
URL: https://mindshub.ai/use-cases

MindsHub agents are AI coworkers you hand outcomes to, not another place to write prompts. Describe the finished thing — a daily briefing, a KPI dashboard, an invoice review pack, a customer feedback memo — and an agent plans the work, calls the right tools and data, runs code in a transparent scratchpad, and returns the artifact. The gallery covers six teams (Ops and admin, Data and analytics, Sales and GTM, Product and engineering, Finance/legal/people, Research and content) with six concrete handoffs each, plus four featured ones at the top. The same pattern underlies all of them: tools and data access, transparent execution, memory across runs, and an open runtime you can host or run locally.

### Consultation
URL: https://mindshub.ai/consultation

A consultation is a free, weekly working session with the MindsHub team — limited spots, no sales pitch. The goal is to help you get to a first working agent for a real task. Bring whatever you have: a use case to brainstorm, an agent to deploy and configure, tools and data to wire up through the credentials vault, a live blocker to troubleshoot, product feedback for the team, or open questions about Hermes, OpenClaw, NanoClaw, Anton, or GBrain. Good for people evaluating agents, just deployed and unsure what is next, hitting a blocker, connecting tools and data, prototyping something new, or scoping a specific use case. Book a session at https://s.mdb.ai/4urmXgW.

### Pricing
URL: https://mindshub.ai/pricing

MindsHub pricing has two doors at one price. Cowork, the unified workspace, is $9.95/month with 5M tokens included — delegate whole tasks and collect finished, shareable work, with no API keys or setup. Running your own open-source agent is $9.95/month per agent, with the Model Router and 5M tokens included as an intro offer, or your own LLM accounts. Both include the Model Router across commercial and open models, with latest:* aliases keeping models current. Early-access pricing while usage-based billing is built; early subscribers keep their intro rate. Billed monthly, cancel anytime. Secured to SOC 2 Type II.

Q: What is MindsHub?
A: MindsHub is the platform for open-source AI agents. Delegate whole tasks in Cowork, the unified workspace, or run your own agent with its native UI and harness.

Q: How much does MindsHub cost?
A: It is $9.95/month with 5M tokens included — whether you use Cowork, the unified workspace, or run your own open-source agent ($9.95/month per agent). Billed monthly, cancel anytime. This is early-access pricing while we build usage-based billing.

Q: What do the 5M tokens cover in practice?
A: Think of it as a generous monthly AI allowance. In everyday use that's plenty of delegated work — for example a weekly competitive digest, a handful of dashboards, a stack of document reviews, and recurring briefings. Heavier or premium-model tasks draw it down faster, and your usage is visible in your account.

Q: Do I need API keys to start?
A: No. The Model Router is wired in, so there are no provider keys to set up. You can connect your own LLM accounts later if you want direct provider control.

Q: What happens when usage-based billing ships?
A: Detailed, usage-based billing is coming soon. We'll publish a transparent rate card before anything changes, and early subscribers keep their intro rate.

Q: Can I switch between Cowork and running my own agent?
A: Yes. One MindsHub account works for both — switch anytime.

Q: Which open-source agents can I run?
A: Anton and Hermes run in Cowork today. OpenClaw, OpenClaw + GBrain, NanoClaw, and Hermes run standalone with their native harness — more on the way.

Q: How do the latest:* aliases work?
A: Instead of pinning a specific model version, reference an alias like latest:sonnet or latest:gpt. The Model Router resolves it to the current pinned version of that family, so you pick up new releases without changes.

### Model Router
URL: https://mindshub.ai/model-router

Model choice is where agents quietly win or lose on cost and quality, and MindsHub makes it a dropdown rather than a project. Agents consume far more tokens than a chat session — they plan, call tools, read results, and iterate over many steps — so running that volume on cost-effective open-source models (DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi) cuts the bill sharply versus frontier pricing. When a step needs the best reasoning available, switch to a frontier model from Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google and back again: the agent stays the same, every task still runs, and your history and memory carry over with nothing to migrate. The Model Router is pre-wired across commercial and open providers, so there are no per-provider API keys to set up — pick a planning model and a coding model from a dropdown, tune the reasoning effort per model, and keep versions current with latest:* aliases. Choosing a different model — and a different agent — per individual task is coming soon. Models are configured in MindsHub Cowork, the unified workspace for open-source agents.

Q: Which models can I use?
A: Frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google, plus the most powerful open-source models — DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi (Moonshot). Pick a planning model and a coding model from a dropdown; the Model Router is pre-wired, so there are no provider API keys to set up.

Q: Why run agents on open-source models?
A: Agents consume far more tokens than a chat session — they plan, call tools, read results, and iterate over many steps. Running that volume on cost-effective open-source models cuts the bill dramatically, and you can still reach for a frontier model on the steps that need it.

Q: If I switch models, do I lose my work?
A: No. The model is a setting under your agent. Switch it and the same agent keeps running — your tasks, history, and memory carry over. There is nothing to migrate or re-set-up.

Q: Do I need API keys?
A: No. The Model Router is wired in across commercial and open models, so there are no provider keys to manage. You can connect your own LLM accounts later if you want direct provider control.

Q: Can I pick a different model per task?
A: Today the model applies across your work. Choosing a different model — and a different agent — per individual task is coming soon.

Q: What are the latest:* aliases?
A: Instead of pinning a specific model version, reference an alias like latest:deepseek or latest:gpt. The Model Router resolves it to the current pinned version of that family, so you pick up new releases without changes.

### MindsHub vs MindsDB
URL: https://mindshub.ai/mindshub-vs-mindsdb

MindsDB started in 2018 with a clear principle: bring AI to the data instead of moving data to the AI. The 'DB' suffix described where the work happened — inside Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB, Snowflake, and the other systems most ML data lived in. When LLMs arrived, the product broadened to cover structured and unstructured information alike — documents, vectors, knowledge bases, federated queries — so AI could reach the full heterogeneous mess of an organization. By 2025 the most interesting AI work was agents that plan, call tools, run code, and ship finished artifacts. We built MindsHub as the platform for open-source AI agents (OpenClaw, NanoClaw, Anton, Hermes) with the operational backbone proprietary offerings keep behind their own walls. The 'DB' suffix had stopped describing what the platform did, and new users kept asking whether MindsDB was itself a database. To remove the ambiguity, the platform rebranded to MindsHub in 2026. The mission, team, company, and commitment to open source are the same; MindsHub is by MindsDB. Old mindsdb.com URLs 301-redirect indefinitely.

Q: Did the company change hands or pivot?
A: No. Same company, same team, same investors. MindsHub is the new product surface; MindsDB is the parent identity. The mission to democratize access to AI is unchanged.

Q: Is the MindsDB query engine going away?
A: No. The query engine and the in-data integrations continue as part of the MindsHub platform — they're part of how agents reach the systems where data lives.

Q: Do old mindsdb.com URLs still work?
A: Yes. Every path on mindsdb.com 301-redirects to the matching path on mindshub.ai. The redirect is in place indefinitely.

Q: What does this change for existing MindsDB users?
A: Nothing about your existing workloads needs to move. The open-source MindsDB project continues. If you want to try open agents on the same platform — OpenClaw, NanoClaw, Anton, Hermes — they're available under the new MindsHub surface.

Q: Why was the old name confusing?
A: The 'DB' suffix made sense when the work happened inside databases. Once the product handled documents, vectors, agent runtimes, and tool-using workflows, the name stopped describing what the platform actually does — and new users kept asking whether MindsDB was itself a database. The rebrand resolves the ambiguity.

### MindsDB Query Engine
URL: https://mindshub.ai/mindsdb-query-engine

MindsDB is the open-source query engine that gives AI agents a single SQL interface to read from every system that holds useful context. The Connect primitive registers any of 200+ sources — Postgres, MySQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, Salesforce, HubSpot, S3, Pinecone, and many more — as a "database" inside MindsDB, then queries them with standard SQL: joins, aggregates, subqueries, the whole vocabulary. The Unify primitive is the Knowledge Base: one CREATE statement turns a folder of PDFs or a Confluence space into a queryable table, with automatic chunking, vectorization, and metadata you choose. The Automate primitive is Jobs and Triggers — schedule a refresh or react to data changes so the query engine stays a live data layer, not a frozen snapshot. MindsDB is open-source, self-hostable, and a standalone project. The same team also offers MindsHub — a separate hosted platform purpose-built for open-source AI agents — which is usually the easier path for teams that just want to run an agent rather than assemble the data layer themselves.

Q: What is MindsDB Query Engine?
A: MindsDB is an open-source SQL query engine that unifies access to 200+ data sources — databases, warehouses, SaaS applications, document stores, and vector indexes — under one SQL dialect. It exposes Knowledge Bases for unstructured data and Jobs / Triggers for automation, so an AI agent has a single, consistent surface to query whatever data it needs.

Q: Is MindsDB still maintained?
A: Yes. MindsDB is actively developed in the open on GitHub (github.com/mindsdb/engine). It is a standalone open-source project that continues to ship features and connectors. For hosted agent building, the same team also offers MindsHub, which is a separate product.

Q: How is MindsDB different from MindsHub?
A: They are two separate products from the same team. MindsDB is a standalone open-source data engine — install it, point it at your sources, and write SQL. MindsHub is a separate hosted platform purpose-built for open-source AI agents (OpenClaw, NanoClaw, Anton, Hermes) with a Model Router, a credentials vault, and an always-on cloud runtime. MindsHub is not built on top of MindsDB; the two are complementary surfaces for different jobs. If you want to build a data layer and an agent runtime yourself, MindsDB is one option; if you want a hosted runtime ready to go, use MindsHub.

Q: How does the query engine compare to a traditional database?
A: MindsDB is not itself a storage engine — it does not own the data. It is a federated query layer that speaks SQL to clients and each source's native protocol to the underlying systems. Think of it as a uniform read/write surface across the systems you already run, rather than a place to copy data into.

Q: How do AI agents use MindsDB?
A: Agents connect to MindsDB once — via SQL or the Model Context Protocol (MCP) — and get a single tool for reading every connected source. Instead of giving the agent one bespoke tool per provider (which blows up the prompt and the failure surface), the agent issues SELECT statements and MindsDB dispatches them to the right handler.

Q: How do Knowledge Bases work?
A: A Knowledge Base is a single CREATE statement that defines an embedding model and a set of metadata columns. MindsDB then handles chunking, vectorization, storage, and re-embedding on updates. You query the Knowledge Base like any table: semantic search via the content column, structured filters via metadata. It collapses a typical RAG stack into one SQL primitive.

Q: Can I self-host MindsDB?
A: Yes. MindsDB is open-source and runs on Linux, macOS, Windows, and Docker. The repo is at github.com/mindsdb/engine. Self-hosting puts you in control of where data flows; the trade-off is operating the runtime yourself rather than letting MindsHub manage it.

Q: Which AI models does MindsDB support?
A: MindsDB is model-neutral. You can plug in Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Hugging Face, or any self-hosted endpoint — both for embeddings inside Knowledge Bases and for LLM-backed queries. Switching providers is a configuration change, not a rewrite.

Q: Where can I find the documentation?
A: Docs are at mindsdb.github.io/engine. Source is at github.com/mindsdb/engine. For the hosted product, see mindshub.ai or read /mindshub-vs-mindsdb for the rebrand story.

### Press Kit
URL: https://mindshub.ai/press-kit

About MindsHub. In 2018, two founders in Berkeley asked why using AI meant copying your data somewhere else. They open-sourced an answer — bring the models to where the data already lives — and the principle held through 500,000+ deployments and a community of builders that grew up around it. MindsHub is the next chapter: as the field moved from one model call to many — with tools, memory, and execution at every step — agents needed somewhere to live and run. MindsHub is that home, with the same open-source ethos and model-neutral foundation, broadened to host the agents (OpenClaw, OpenClaw + GBrain, NanoClaw, Anton, Hermes) the community is building in the open. By MindsDB. Founded 2018 in Berkeley; 39,000+ GitHub stars; pronounced minds-hub. Assets: twelve logo variants ship as SVG and convert to PNG on download (horizontal and stacked color lockups, monochrome black/white, on-brand, an icon-only bear, and a standalone wordmark). The color palette is aqua-led with frost neutrals and four signal accents (Cobalt, Sage, Clay, Citrine). The typography stack is Arimo for display and headlines, Noto Sans for body and UI, Menlo for code and metadata. Voice & tone: plain, technical, and slightly understated. MindsHub sounds the way good engineering sounds — precise, low-drama, and unimpressed by hype. Three rules. Precise over clever: pick the true line over the clever one; the audience is technical and can tell the difference (say "Run open-source agents with real tool access, memory, and credentials," not "Unleash the magic of agentic AI"). Concrete over abstract: prefer verbs that describe what actually happens — connect, route, host, query, infer — over abstractions like "leverage" or "synergize" (say "Connect Postgres. Route inference. Persist memory across runs," not "Unlock enterprise-grade AI capabilities at scale"). Open over closed: lead with what is available now, not what is gated behind a sales call (say "Fork an agent. Read the merge thread," not "Contact us to learn more"). One-liner (use as-is): "MindsHub is the platform for open-source AI agents — where they live, learn, and get things done. Delegate tasks through Cowork, the unified workspace, or run any agent with its native harness." Boilerplate (~100 words): "MindsHub is the platform for open-source AI agents: the place where they live, run, and do real work. At its center is Cowork, the unified workspace where knowledge workers delegate entire tasks — research, analysis, reporting, scheduled operations — and collect finished, shareable results. Builders can just as easily run any open agent with its native UI and harness. Underneath it all: a credentials vault, model routing across commercial and open providers, artifact publishing, persistent memory, and collaboration. Open by design — swap the agent, switch the model, and keep everything you have built. By MindsDB. Founded 2018 in Berkeley. Backed by Benchmark, Mayfield, Y Combinator, and NVIDIA." Press inquiries: see the contact details on the press-kit page, or use the form at /contact.

### Careers
URL: https://mindshub.ai/careers

We are a remote-first team building open-source AI infrastructure for agents, data, and the people who put them to work. Backed by Benchmark, Mayfield, Y Combinator, and NVIDIA. We hire continuously across engineering, product, design, marketing, and customer-facing roles. Benefits include unlimited PTO, generous compensation, medical/dental/vision (US) or equivalent regional plans, mental-health support and wellbeing budget, personal-development budget, home-office budget, company off-sites, and flexible scheduling. We work async-first, with deep-work hours and small teams that own surfaces end-to-end. What we look for: strong taste in the work, a bias toward writing things down, people who can hold a strong opinion and change it when evidence shifts. Past credentials matter less than what you've shipped. Don't see your role listed? Tell us what you want to build at /contact.
